title: Impact of National Wages Council 's 2020 Wage Cut Advisory on Salaries
what_it_is: Impact of National Wages Council 's 2020 Wage Cut Advisory on Salaries

sections.label: Wage adjustments vary across sectors
sections.summary: The NWC expects wage adjustments over the next 12 months to vary across sectors and firms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The NWC expects wage adjustments in the next 12 months to vary across sectors and firms.

sections.label: Management lead wage cuts
sections.summary: A key principle is for management to lead in taking wage cuts and accept steeper cuts than asked of workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: A key principle is for management to take the lead in taking wage cuts and to accept steeper cuts than what they ask of their workers.

sections.label: Wage freeze below $1,400
sections.summary: The Supplementary Guidelines recommend employers freeze wages rather than cut wages for workers earning below $1,400 if needed to avoid retrenchment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, the Supplementary Guidelines recommend that for workers earning below $1,400, employers should, if necessary to avoid retrenchment, freeze wages rather than cut wages.

sections.label: Concerns over Guidelines signalling effect
sections.summary: Concerns arose about the Guidelines' signalling effect causing more pay cuts than necessary and potential abuse by opportunistic firms, raising how to ensure fair implementation and timely wage restoration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: There were a lot of concerns on the ground about the signalling effect of the Guidelines, which may result in more widespread pay cuts than necessary because there is this Guideline, and the potential abuse by some opportunistic firms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, how do we ensure that companies implement wage cuts fairly and reasonably, and restore wages in tandem with business recovery in a timely manner?

sections.label: NWC set out principles
sections.summary: The NWC decided the most reasonable approach was to set out principles, articulating six, the first being that companies should utilise flexibility under the Flexible Wage System.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The NWC ultimately decided that the most reasonable way of going about its Guidelines was to set out a certain set of principles.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The principles that they clearly articulated were six: firstly, whichever company in whichever sector, should utilise the range of flexibility under the Flexible Wage System.

sections.label: Wage adjustments negotiated and agreed
sections.summary: The sixth principle is that wage adjustments should be negotiated and agreed with the union if one exists, or directly with employees if not.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The sixth principle that the NWC articulated is that these wage adjustments should be negotiated and agreed upon if there is a union in the company, and if there is no union, the employer should do so directly with the employees.

sections.label: Workfare Special Payment top-ups
sections.summary: Additional top-ups were intended where necessary, and this year's Workfare Special Payment's two tranches have been paid out.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It has been our intention wherever necessary to provide additional top-ups to help these workers tide over this period of difficulty.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This year, there was a Workfare Special Payment made, both tranches have already been paid out.
